# Phase 16: attention traces and the offline oracle study

Upgrade plan items A2 (trace recorder) and A3 (offline replay with an optimal oracle); see
[GAP_TABLE.md](../GAP_TABLE.md) for why they were taken first and how their scope was narrowed.

## What was built

- `lazykv/trace.py`: `TraceRecorder`, a decode-time view over a prefilled full cache that attends
  densely (the decode is the full cache's own) and records, at every decode step, in every selecting
  layer and for every KV head, the **true attention mass** of every block (float32 softmax over the
  whole KV, averaged over the head's query group) and the **Quest bound** of every candidate block,
  the one rungs 5 to 8 rank by. Traces save to `.npz`.
- `lazykv/residency_sim.py`: offline replay. Four selectors (the true-mass oracle, the Quest-style
  bound, the previous step's true top-K, and the most recent K) scored by the mass they capture,
  and two slot-replacement rules (the tier's least-recently-selected LRU, and Belady) scored by
  fetches.
- `scripts/06_record_traces.py`, `scripts/analyze_phase16.py`, `configs/phase16.yaml`.

**How the simulator was checked against the runtime** (`tests/test_trace.py`,
`tests/test_residency_sim.py`):

- Replaying the tier's own recorded selection through the simulated LRU reproduces the tier's
  per-step fetch counts exactly.
- The simulated Quest selection picks the same bound values as `top_blocks` live; the block ids can
  differ only at exact ties (below).
- Belady matches an exhaustive search for the minimum fetch count on 40 random small instances, and
  never fetches more than LRU.
- Recording leaves the decode bit-identical, and each head's mass sums to one.

## The run

45 NIAH prompts at
32,768 tokens, the exact prompts Phase 8 ran rung 5 on, plus
2 teacher-forced windows; Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct, 64-token
blocks. The full cache's answers here match Phase 8's on
45 of
45 prompts, so the join with Phase 8's per-prompt
results below is on the same decode.

**Which steps mean what.** A trace follows the full cache's trajectory. On the first answer token
the query is the same under every policy, so that column is exact for each selector. Later NIAH
tokens and the teacher-forced windows show the selectors on the reference trajectory.

## 1. Selection: how much of the true attention mass each selector captures

Mass captured per (step, layer, KV head), averaged; sink and current block always included, as in
every selecting rung. The first-answer-token column has a 95% bootstrap CI over prompts.

| Budget | K | Selector | NIAH, first answer token | NIAH, later tokens | NIAH, 5th percentile cell | Teacher-forced |
| --- | --: | --- | --: | --: | --: | --: |
| 75% | 382 | Oracle (true top-K) | 99.61% (99.59–99.63) | 99.70% | 98.9% | 99.58% |
|  |  | Quest-style bound | 98.98% (98.91–99.03) | 99.23% | 97.3% | 98.74% |
|  |  | Previous step's true top-K | same as Quest (falls back to it) | 99.57% | 98.3% | 99.37% |
|  |  | Most recent K | 94.17% (93.35–94.95) | 96.15% | 85.8% | 96.71% |
| 50% | 254 | Oracle (true top-K) | 98.50% (98.43–98.57) | 98.82% | 96.2% | 98.27% |
|  |  | Quest-style bound | 96.87% (96.72–97.00) | 97.59% | 92.2% | 96.09% |
|  |  | Previous step's true top-K | same as Quest (falls back to it) | 98.46% | 94.7% | 97.68% |
|  |  | Most recent K | 90.35% (89.45–91.28) | 93.82% | 77.5% | 94.76% |
| 25% | 126 | Oracle (true top-K) | 95.88% (95.71–96.05) | 96.72% | 90.2% | 94.97% |
|  |  | Quest-style bound | 92.97% (92.67–93.26) | 94.50% | 83.7% | 91.13% |
|  |  | Previous step's true top-K | same as Quest (falls back to it) | 96.06% | 87.7% | 93.85% |
|  |  | Most recent K | 84.27% (83.25–85.22) | 89.33% | 65.5% | 88.07% |
| 12.5% | 62 | Oracle (true top-K) | 93.03% (92.76–93.29) | 94.40% | 84.1% | 91.13% |
|  |  | Quest-style bound | 89.41% (88.97–89.82) | 91.70% | 76.5% | 86.65% |
|  |  | Previous step's true top-K | same as Quest (falls back to it) | 93.61% | 81.4% | 89.78% |
|  |  | Most recent K | 81.94% (80.91–82.91) | 87.56% | 62.2% | 85.38% |
| 6.25% | 30 | Oracle (true top-K) | 90.35% (90.02–90.69) | 92.23% | 78.8% | 87.49% |
|  |  | Quest-style bound | 86.38% (85.86–86.90) | 89.38% | 70.8% | 83.10% |
|  |  | Previous step's true top-K | same as Quest (falls back to it) | 91.45% | 76.0% | 86.16% |
|  |  | Most recent K | 80.42% (79.38–81.41) | 86.44% | 60.2% | 83.54% |

- **Quest-style selection is close to the selection ceiling, and further from it as the budget
  shrinks.** At the first answer token it captures
  95.6%–99.4%
  of what the oracle captures across budgets; at
  6.25% that is
  86.4% of the mass against the oracle's
  90.4% and recency's
  80.4%.
- **The previous step's true attention is a better selector than the bound.** On later tokens it
  captures +0.3 pp to
  +2.1 pp more mass than Quest on NIAH, and
  +0.6 pp to
  +3.1 pp on the teacher-forced windows. That
  matters for the one speed direction Phases 4 to 11 left open, a residency decision made on the GPU
  without a per-layer host round trip: last step's attention is already on the GPU. **The caveat is
  large and stated here:** this is an upper bound. A sparse decode only computes attention over the
  blocks it attended, so a real stale selector sees last step's mass on those blocks alone.
- **The bound ties at the K-th place more often than not.** In
  66%–86%
  of (step, layer, head) cells, depending on the budget, the K-th and (K+1)-th highest bounds are
  equal in bf16, the dtype the runtime ranks in. Which block gets the last places is then decided by
  `topk`'s tie order, not by the bound. How much mass a float32 bound would recover there is
  not measured.

## 2. Captured mass does not predict which answers are lost

Per budget, Phase 8's rung 5 answers on the same prompts, split into prompts where it kept the full
cache's score and prompts where it lost some; the mass Quest captured at the first answer token in
each group. AUC is the probability that a kept prompt captured more mass than a lost one: 0.5 is no
signal. Prompts the full cache misses are left out.

| Budget | Prompts kept | Prompts lost | Quest mass, kept | Quest mass, lost | Oracle mass, lost | AUC |
| --- | --: | --: | --: | --: | --: | --: |
| 75% | 42 | 2 | 98.98% | 98.91% | 99.62% | 0.69 |
| 50% | 39 | 5 | 96.87% | 96.91% | 98.56% | 0.50 |
| 25% | 34 | 10 | 92.89% | 93.30% | 96.11% | 0.40 |
| 12.5% | 26 | 18 | 89.11% | 89.91% | 93.51% | 0.36 |
| 6.25% | 17 | 27 | 86.50% | 86.35% | 90.52% | 0.53 |

**Negative result.** AUC runs
0.36–0.69
across budgets, on both sides of 0.5 with no consistent direction: mass averaged over every
selecting layer and head does not tell which prompts Quest-style selection gets wrong. The prompts it
lost captured about as much mass as the ones it kept, and at some budgets more.
This is the same lesson as Phase 10's perplexity result, one level down: an average over the whole
cache does not see the few blocks and heads retrieval depends on. Two limits on how far it goes:
the lost groups at the loosest budgets are small, and only the first answer token is policy-exact.

It changes how the upgrade plan can be carried out. The plan says to tune a working-set selector's
weights (A5) on this simulator by mass captured. On this evidence, mass captured is not a quality
target, and tuning to it would optimize something NIAH does not reward. A per-head or
needle-position measure is the next thing to try, and it needs the owner's go-ahead.

- **With exactly K slots the rule cannot matter**, as predicted in the gap table: every slot outside
  the current selection must go. LRU and Belady fetch identically in every such condition
  (`forced_case_identical`: True).
- **With spare slots, Belady fetches
  0.45–0.64×
  what LRU does.** But Phases 4, 5 and 7
  measured that fetch traffic is not what decode time is spent on (the host round trip is), so this is
  a ceiling on bytes moved, not on speed. It would matter on a link slower than this laptop's, or once
  the host round trip is gone.

## What this phase does not show

- One model (1B), one context (32K), 45 prompts, two teacher-forced windows.
- Mass is averaged over each KV head's query group; Quest ranks by the group maximum.
- The stale-oracle result is an upper bound (above), and nothing here was timed.
